title.es: Episodio de pódcast: escuchar, resumir, responder

es: Escuchar un episodio de pódcast, resumirlo con fidelidad, señalar una implicación y añadir una reacción propia con matiz, separando lo dicho, lo insinuado y lo que tú opinas.

vocabulary.es: lo que me llamó la atención

teaching.en: In this episode, the host asked her guest about working from home, and the guest came across as thoughtful rather than certain.
teaching.es: En este episodio, la presentadora preguntó a su invitada por el teletrabajo, y la invitada dio la impresión de ser reflexiva más que segura.
teaching.explanationEs: Come across as + adjetivo describe la impresión que da alguien; host y guest organizan el episodio.
segments: In this episode, the host asked her guest about working from
home, and the guest came across as thoughtful rather than certain.
teaching.audioText: In this episode, the host asked her guest about working from home, and the guest came across as thoughtful rather than certain.

teaching.en: What struck me was that the guest never said the job was easy, although the host kept inviting her to.
teaching.es: Lo que me llamó la atención fue que la invitada nunca dijo que el trabajo fuera fácil, aunque la presentadora la invitaba a ello.
teaching.explanationEs: What struck me was… introduce lo que te llamó la atención, incluso lo que no se dijo.
segments: What struck me was that the guest never said the
job was easy, although the host kept inviting her to.

teaching.en: Her answers did not say so, yet they seem to imply that the change was harder than the host wanted to admit.
teaching.es: Sus respuestas no lo decían, pero parecen dar a entender que el cambio fue más difícil de lo que la presentadora quería admitir.
teaching.explanationEs: Seem to imply señala una implicación sin afirmarla: lo insinuado no es lo dicho.
segments: Her answers did not say so, yet they seem to imply
that the change was harder than the host wanted to admit.
teaching.audioText: Her answers did not say so, yet they seem to imply that the change was harder than the host wanted to admit.

teaching.en: I do not want to read into a single pause too much, but the guest hesitated before every mention of the office.
teaching.es: No quiero interpretar de más una sola pausa, pero la invitada dudó antes de cada mención de la oficina.
teaching.explanationEs: Read into = atribuir un significado que quizá no está; se usa con cautela.

much, but the guest hesitated before every mention of the office.

teaching.en: To be fair, the host made a fair point, yet I take issue with the claim that the guest had simply changed her mind.
teaching.es: Para ser justos, la presentadora hizo una observación razonable, pero discrepo de que la invitada simplemente hubiera cambiado de opinión.
teaching.explanationEs: To be fair reconoce lo bueno; take issue with introduce un desacuerdo concreto y educado.
segments: To be fair, the host made a fair point, yet I take
issue with the claim that the guest had simply changed her mind.

teaching.en: A gut reaction is rarely the last word, so I agree up to a point and I would add one doubt about the episode.
teaching.es: Una reacción instintiva rara vez es la última palabra, así que estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto y añadiría una duda sobre el episodio.
teaching.explanationEs: Up to a point matiza el acuerdo; I would add suma un punto propio sin negar lo anterior.

prompt.es: Separa lo dicho de lo insinuado: ¿qué deja entrever la directora?

choices.text: That she doubts the team is ready.
That the client asked for far too much.
That the team finished the work early.

feedback.es: Cumplir lo pedido y añadir «we will see» no promete nada: insinúa dudas sobre si el equipo está listo.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que no promete.

origin.text: Asked whether her team was ready for the launch, the manager said: We have done everything the client asked, and we will see.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que me llamó la atención fue que la invitada nunca dijera que fuera fácil.»

feedback.es: What struck me was… introduce lo que te llamó la atención, aunque sea algo que no se dijo.

origin.text: What ___ me was that the guest never said working from home was easy, even when the host asked her twice.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la capa del comentario a la que pertenece.

pairs: The host asked whether it is better.
Her answer seemed to imply a doubt.
To be fair, I agree up to a point.
I would add that not everyone has a quiet room.

feedback.es: Cada frase ocupa una capa distinta: lo dicho, lo insinuado, la reacción propia y lo que tú añades.

hint.es: Pregúntate si la frase cuenta, sugiere u opina.

pairs: The host asked whether it is better.

I would add that not everyone has a quiet room.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué insinúa la invitada con su respuesta.

choices.text: That the team was split evenly over the experiment.
That those who did not volunteer may disagree.
That the host had not understood the experiment.

feedback.es: Responde solo por quienes se ofrecieron: insinúa que los demás podrían no estar de acuerdo; no habla de un equipo dividido por igual.

origin.audio: The guest said that the experiment was a success. The host asked whether everyone on the team would agree. After a pause, the guest said that those who had asked to take part certainly would. The host smiled but did not press her.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor de la reseña?

choices.text: Not persuaded by the case for flexible hours, though polite about it.
Fully persuaded, with only a small point of wording to correct.
Partly persuaded, but not ready to accept such a sweeping claim.

feedback.es: Reconoce el mérito del argumento («to be fair») pero discrepa de una afirmación demasiado general; no la rechaza por completo ni la acepta salvo un detalle de redacción.

origin.text: To be fair, the guest made a strong case for flexible hours. Still, I take issue with her claim that commuting is always wasted time: many people I know use the train to read, think or switch off.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su respuesta parecía dar a entender que el cambio fue difícil.»

answer.text: Her answer seemed to imply that the change was difficult

feedback.es: Seemed to imply + that + oración formula lo insinuado sin afirmarlo.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y escribe un resumen con una implicación y tu reacción.

answer.text: In this episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher, whether it is better to work from home. According to the guest, it depends. First, many people save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and she called this a real benefit. Second, she said that some people feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. Third, she suggested that companies could offer two office days a week, which she described as a fair compromise. When the host asked whether working at home is better, she answered that it is not exactly better, which seemed to imply that the answer is not a simple yes. What struck me was that she never said it is easy. To be fair, I found the episode balanced, and I see her point about the benefits. However, I would add one doubt of my own: two office days a week may be hard to organise for small firms, so the compromise may suit large companies better. My gut reaction was to agree with her up to a point. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I would like to hear how companies respond.

My gut reaction was to agree with her up to a point. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I would like to hear how companies respond.

This episode of the podcast was about working from home. The host asked her guest whether it is better, and the guest explained that it depends. On the positive side, many people save two hours a day because they no longer travel to an office. On the negative side, some of them feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. She suggested that a good compromise could be two office days a week. The host asked again whether working at home is better, and the guest replied not exactly, which implied that the situation is more complicated than a simple yes or no. My reaction is positive: to be fair, she did not try to sell one answer, and what struck me was how honest she was about the problems. However, I would add that two office days a week could be hard to organise for small firms, and that could make the compromise less useful for them. Overall, I agree with her up to a point, and I would like to hear how companies respond to her ideas.

feedback.es: El texto resume lo dicho con fidelidad, detecta la implicación de «not exactly», reacciona con matiz y cierra con una conclusión.

origin.text: Escucha el episodio (puedes oírlo varias veces) y escribe en inglés, de unas 180 a 260 palabras, una reseña: resume las ideas de la invitada (atribúyelas), señala una implicación, añade tu reacción con un matiz (to be fair, I would add…) y termina con una frase de cierre. No inventes datos.
origin.audio: In this week's episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher who studies remote work, whether working from home is better. The guest said that it depends. Many people, she explained, save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and that is a real benefit. Asked whether it is therefore better, she answered: not exactly. Some people told her that they feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. The host asked whether there is a solution, and the guest suggested, after a slight pause, that companies could offer two office days a week, which she called a fair compromise. She added that not everyone has a quiet room at home, a point that she said is often overlooked. The host thanked her and promised to return to the subject.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y elige qué sugiere la invitada con «not exactly».

choices.text: That the answer is not as simple as yes.
That she thinks the host's question is badly phrased.
That working from home is worse than working in an office.

feedback.es: «Not exactly» es un no amable: da a entender que la respuesta no es un sí sencillo; no critica la pregunta ni afirma que el teletrabajo sea peor, porque después ofrece un compromiso.

prompt.es: Completa: «Discrepo de su afirmación de que toda empresa debería permitir el teletrabajo.»

feedback.es: Take issue with + afirmación es la fórmula educada para discrepar de algo concreto.

origin.text: I agree with much of what the guest said, but I take ___ with her claim that every company should allow remote work.

prompt.es: ¿Qué impresión da la invitada, según el autor?

choices.text: Thoughtful, but not ready to admit what the research could not show.
Careful, and honest about what her evidence could show.
Warm but impatient with the host's questions.

feedback.es: La invitada «came across as careful rather than evasive» porque admitió lo que la investigación no podía demostrar; la impaciencia es de la presentadora, no de ella.

origin.text: The host came across as warm but slightly impatient: she thanked the guest twice, yet she interrupted the last answer to ask about the next topic. The guest, for her part, came across as careful rather than evasive, since she admitted what the research could not show.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el autor sobre los costes para las empresas?

choices.text: That the guest purposely hid the real costs from her listeners.
That the costs are too small to be worth giving a figure.
That the guest's long answer left listeners no better informed about costs.

feedback.es: El autor dice que la respuesta fue larga pero sin cifras y que terminó sabiendo menos; aclara expresamente que no acusa a la invitada de ocultar nada.

origin.text: I liked the episode, and the guest was charming. But when the host asked about the costs to companies, the answer took four minutes and contained no number. I am not saying that she was hiding something; I am saying that I finished listening knowing less about costs than when I began.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para ser justos, la invitada nunca dijo que todas pudieran costearlo.»

feedback.es: To be fair introduce un matiz a favor de la otra persona antes de seguir con la crítica.

origin.text: I doubt that every company can afford it. To be ___, though, the guest never said that they could, and that is a point worth remembering.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Yo añadiría que las empresas pequeñas podrían tener problemas con el coste.»

answer.text: I would add that small companies may struggle with the cost

feedback.es: I would add + that introduce tu aportación sin contradecir lo dicho por otro.
